from_quote: Congress shall have power to dispose of and make all needful rules and regulations respecting the territory or other property of the United States
rationale: Cites "The 3d section, in article IV" and reproduces this clause closely.
to_quote: The Congress shall have Power to dispose of and make all needful Rules and Regulations respecting the Territory or other Property belonging to the United States

from_quote: the words of the constitution are, "All Powers Herein Granted."
rationale: Quotes in quotation marks "All Powers Herein Granted" as "the words of the constitution," from this clause.

from_quote: The United States shall guarantee to every state in the Union a Republican Form of Governmcnt; and shall protect each of them against invasion; and on application of the legislature, or of the executive (when the legislature cannot be convened) against domestic violence.
rationale: Cites "Section 4, of article IV" and reproduces this clause verbatim ("Governmcnt" is OCR damage).
to_quote: The United States shall guarantee to every State in this Union a Republican Form of Government, and shall protect each of them against Invasion; and on Application of the Legislature, or of the Executive (when the Legislature cannot be convened) against domestic Violence.

from_quote: That Congress, whenever two-thirds of both houses shall deem it necessary, shall propose amendments to this constitution; or on the application of the legislatures of two-thirds of the states, shall call a convention for proposing amendments
rationale: Cites "Article V." and reproduces the whole article nearly verbatim.
to_quote: The Congress, whenever two thirds of both Houses shall deem it necessary, shall propose Amendments to this Constitution, or, on the Application of the Legislatures of two thirds of the several States, shall call a Convention for proposing Amendments

from_quote: The 5th article also provides, that the states may propose any alterations which they see fit
rationale: Cites "The 5th article" and says alterations "must be ratified by three-fourths of the states," referring to the article quoted in the preceding paragraph.

from_quote: shall be the supreme law of the land, and the judges in every state shall be bound thereby, anything in the constitution or laws of any state to the contrary notwithstanding.
rationale: Reproduces this clause closely, introduced as what "The 6th section provides" (it is the second clause of Article VI).
to_quote: shall be the supreme Law of the Land; and the Judges in every State shall be bound thereby, any Thing in the Constitution or Laws of any State to the Contrary notwithstanding.

from_quote: the senators and representatives before mentioned, and the members of the several state legislatures and all executive and judicial officers, both of the United States and of the several states, shall be bound, by oath or affirmation, to support this constitution ; but no religious test shall ever be required as a qualification to any office or publick trust under the United States.
rationale: Reproduces this clause verbatim; the passage introduces it as "Article IV." although the clause is in Article VI.
to_quote: The Senators and Representatives before mentioned, and the Members of the several State Legislatures, and all executive and judicial Officers, both of the United States and of the several States, shall be bound by Oath or Affirmation, to support this Constitution; but no religious Test shall ever be required as a Qualification to any Office or public Trust under the United States.

from_quote: in order to form a more perfect Union, establish justice, insure domestick tranquillity, provide for the common defence, promote the general welfare, and secure the blessings of liberty to ourselves and our posterity,
rationale: Quotes the Preamble's words in quotation marks, and its "ordain and establish" separately.
to_quote: in Order to form a more perfect Union, establish Justice, insure domestic Tranquility, provide for the common defence, promote the general Welfare, and secure the Blessings of Liberty to ourselves and our Posterity
